headline: US prosecutors have charged a California man with smuggling more than 300 million dollars of AI servers to China through Malaysia and Singapore.
score_reason: A large export-control prosecution, but the arrest and announcement came on 30 Sep and 1 Oct 2026, before today's window.
importance_line: The case shows the US is prosecuting chip smuggling at the hundreds-of-millions scale and names the Southeast Asia transit route, which matters to chip makers and exporters, though the charges are allegations the defendant has not yet answered in court.
summary: The Next Web reports that the US Justice Department charged Greg Lui, 38, of San Gabriel, California, with using his company Earthmade Computer to ship more than 300 million dollars of servers packed with US-made AI graphics processors to China in 2023 and 2024, routing them through Malaysia and Singapore with false paperwork to avoid export licences; the arrest was on 30 Sep 2026 and the announcement on 1 Oct 2026. He faces three counts, including smuggling and money-laundering conspiracy, with up to 50 years in prison if convicted, and the indictment is an allegation he is presumed innocent of; US attorney Bill Essayli said, "We will aggressively prosecute those who put our national security at risk for profit."
notes: Score lowered from 7 to 6: event before 3 Oct 2026. TNW's own write-up, also covered by Reuters.
